keys.description: The PUBLIC API this service forwards every built-in tool to, with the caller's own key. It never reaches past the gateway.
The port the MCP transport listens on; the gateway's MCP_URL points here.
Bind address. Container-internal only — the gateway is the edge.

`production` closes /docs, /redoc and /openapi.json on the PUBLIC app. Note the ASSEMBLER still reads each DOMAIN's OpenAPI over the internal network to derive tool schemas — that is a different app's docs, on a different edge.
Declared Jitsi hosts for meeting-link parsing — the SAME setting meeting-api reads, because two parsers that disagree about what a link is accept different meetings.
identity's base URL. A domain whose URL is set is ASKED for its tool manifest; one whose URL is unset is never asked and its tools are absent. Identity is the one domain everyone may depend on.
meetings' base URL, on the same terms.
flows' base URL, on the same terms.

flows' own operator key, forwarded as X-Flows-Operator-Key on the two admin-gated tools (flows_submit, flow_lifecycle — core/flows/mcp.tools.v1.json's `auth: admin`). Their doors read ONLY this key, never the caller's own credential, so unset alongside a set FLOWS_API_URL is a deployment whose facts assembly refuses to publish (manifest.py's admin-key check fails the boot) rather than list two tools their own door would 401.
agent's base URL, on the same terms. Unset is the no-agents deployment, which is a product and not a degraded state.

A directory a private deployment mounts its own tool manifests into — billing, seats, entitlement. Assembled identically to the OSS ones and competing for names in the same space, so a mount can COLLIDE but never SHADOW. EMPTY IS THE OSS PRODUCT, exactly.

Where `report_issue` files an agent-written ticket. POINT IT AT A DEDICATED TICKETS REPO: ticket bodies are third-party text, and an operational repo's issues are read as work signal by planning loops.
Credential for that sink. Fine-grained, SINGLE-REPO, issues:write only, from a secret store.
`raw` (default) POSTs the ticket JSON to an opaque webhook; `github` maps it onto POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues so an issue tracker IS the sink.
Salt for the caller fingerprint that dedupes tickets. A deployment SHOULD set its own so fingerprints are not comparable across deployments.

assembly.description: Assembling one MCP surface from the tool manifests of the domains this deployment carries (PRD decision 40). Each domain serves its own manifest and its OpenAPI; this service asks, refuses the combinations that cannot be right, and presents the union.
assembly.when_unconfigured: No domain is asked, so the surface is exactly this service's own built-in tools. That is a smaller product, never a broken one — a tool whose domain is absent is ABSENT from tools/list rather than present-and-failing.

private_domains.description: A paid or private domain composing onto this line without a line of it living in this repo: its manifest is mounted, discovered and assembled like any other.
private_domains.when_unconfigured: There are no mounted manifests, which IS the OSS product. This repo never carries a gate shipped dark.

ticket_sink.description: `report_issue` — an agent filing a ticket a human reads.
ticket_sink.when_unconfigured: `report_issue` answers 503 `not configured` and nothing else changes.
